summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted with a five-day history of cough, diarrhea, myalgias, and low-grade fevers. He was found to have parainfluenza type 3 infection, with chest imaging showing interstitial lung changes consistent with viral or atypical infection. His kidney function was acutely worsened on admission, likely due to dehydration from poor oral intake and diarrhea, but improved with intravenous fluids. He was managed supportively with oxygen, cough control, and a short course of levofloxacin. Acyclovir was held due to impaired renal function. His symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue hydration, monitor weight, and follow up with his oncologist.
